parsed.statement: The CC4 dashboard and SQLite metrics store shall serve as the reference implementation of the observability substrate for Seldon, Wintermute, and related infrastructure, using an insert-only schema with dot-notation metric names, JSON dimensions, and versioning by collected_by. When adjacent or future observability work is undertaken, it shall extend the CC4 metrics store rather than build parallel stores. Every gate, sleep function, and pipeline step that claims value shall emit events to the substrate. A new Seldon or Wintermute component shall not be considered complete unless it emits appropriate events to the substrate, as a definition-of-done criterion. When substrate data is available, decisions about component retention, deprecation, and calibration — including whether a gate is catching violations, whether a function is producing signal, or whether a pipeline is used — shall be made against that substrate data rather than qualitative recall.

parsed.statement: The seldon project-init bootstrap state shall be defined as data in YAML template files under seldon/templates/, loaded by seldon.templates.loader, with each template schema requiring at minimum a name key matching the filename stem, a description string, and a bootstrap_tasks list (which may be empty) of task entries each containing a description string and an optional name string, while unrecognized top-level keys shall be preserved in the loaded dict. The seldon init <project_name> command shall accept a --template <name> option defaulting to blank to select which template to apply, a --list-templates option to enumerate available templates and exit, and a --force option to proceed even if the target Neo4j database already contains artifacts. The seldon init command shall record the selected template name at project.template in the generated seldon.yaml. The seldon templates shipped shall include blank, an empty default template for projects where the user writes their own tasks, and paper, containing the five SETUP-01 through SETUP-05 manuscript tasks, selectable via --template paper. The seldon init command shall verify that the target Neo4j database contains no Artifact nodes before proceeding and shall fail loudly if it does, unless the --force option is specified to override this check for explicit re-init.

parsed.statement: Within a repo-scoped Seldon instance, sub-projects shall be first-class graph artifacts represented as Subproject nodes storing slug, name, document_type, paths, conventions, state, timestamps, and optional description, while seldon.yaml shall be reduced to bootstrap-only configuration (event_store, neo4j, project, shared_ontology, and optional repo-wide conventions) with all sub-project-specific metadata held in the graph. Every non-ontology, non-repo-wide artifact (including ResearchTask, PaperSection, Result, Issue, and DesignNote) shall carry an explicit BELONGS_TO edge to exactly one Subproject node, and artifacts with no BELONGS_TO edge shall be treated as repo-scoped. The Seldon system shall prohibit direct edges between artifacts belonging to different sub-projects, requiring cross-sub-project relationships to route through the central ontology or through an explicit repo-scoped CrossReference artifact naming both endpoints, and seldon verify shall check for violations of this isolation invariant. Sub-projects shall own their own cc_tasks/, handoffs/, audits/, and CLAUDE.md directories, and the migration for brock_projects shall move existing flat top-level cc_tasks/ and handoffs/ content into the sfv-paper sub-project directory. Every event written after this decision shall carry a subproject_slug field, which shall be null for repo-scoped events. When seldon go is invoked at the repo root, the system shall return a repo dashboard listing Subproject nodes, states, last-updated times, and open task counts; when invoked inside a sub-project directory, the system shall auto-scope to that sub-project's CLAUDE.md, latest handoff, open tasks, and audit pipeline; and seldon go shall support an explicit --subproject <slug> override from any location. The CLI shall provide a subproject command group (add, list, show, update) with promote deferred as a documented future feature not built in v1, and existing commands (task, issue, cc, paper, verify) shall gain scope awareness via cwd detection or a --subproject flag, auto-creating BELONGS_TO edges as needed. Existing MCP tools shall gain an optional subproject parameter that, when omitted, is inferred from cwd or otherwise causes the tool to operate repo-wide or return a specify-subproject error. Ontology terms, repo-level ADs, and migration events shall not receive BELONGS_TO edges, as they are repo-wide by design.

parsed.statement: The seldon.core.artifacts schema shall define a `snapshot: bool` artifact property, defaulting to false, declared on the `Script`, `DataFile`, and `PaperSection` types that carry `content_hash` with a path in research.yaml, representing that the artifact records a file as it stood at registration while the live file is expected to diverge from that recorded content_hash. The seldon.core.artifacts validator shall accept only a real Python bool for the `snapshot` property on both create and update. The CLI shall parse a `-p snapshot=true|false|1|0|yes|no` argument (case-insensitive) into a bool, and shall pass through any other literal unchanged so that the validator refuses it. When verify runs the drift comparison, the verify command shall skip snapshot artifacts from drift checking, shall exclude them from the tracked-file count N, and shall report them informationally in the same summary line in the form "All N tracked files in sync — K snapshot artifacts, drift not checked." The `--fix` command shall never compute or write a hash for a snapshot artifact, shall delegate to `paper sync`, and `sync_section` shall return a status of `snapshot` for a flagged artifact without computing or writing a hash; `paper sync` shall report the count of such artifacts. When a path resolves to a directory, the verify command shall report it as "N path(s) resolve to a directory (schema violation): <path> (<type> <id8>)", shall continue the check, and shall set the result to `fixable=False` unless real drift is also present.

parsed.statement: The seldon domain model shall define `precedes` as a many-to-many relationship type from ResearchTask to ResearchTask, with an optional `reason` property and an inverse read-name `preceded_by` that is never written as an edge; `DomainConfig` shall reject any configuration in which a declared inverse name is also declared as a relationship type. The system shall store `precedes` edges in one direction only. `RelationshipConfig` shall support `cardinality`, `inverse`, and `properties` fields, and edge property validation shall be opt-in: a relationship type declaring no property schema shall accept any properties, while a type declaring a schema shall have its properties validated against that schema. The seldon.core.artifacts.create_link function shall enforce, before appending any event, that the `precedes` subgraph has no self-loop and no cycle, rejecting a write that would create either; on rejection of a cycle, the system shall report the shortest path that would close the cycle. All write paths that create `precedes` edges, including `seldon task precede`, `seldon task chain`, the three MCP tools, and `seldon link create`, shall route through this gate. The `seldon task chain` command shall write a given sequence of consecutive task pairs as a single all-or-nothing operation, validating each pair against the existing graph plus prior pairs in the same call before any write occurs, and shall skip an edge that already exists rather than duplicate it. A predecessor ResearchTask shall be considered satisfied when its state is `completed`, `verified`, `superseded`, or `withdrawn`, and shall be considered not satisfied when its state is `rejected` or when its node is missing; `seldon verify` shall report a missing predecessor endpoint as a separate dangling-endpoint finding. Enforcement of `precedes` shall be advisory only: `seldon go` and `task list` shall treat it as advisory, and a state transition moving a successor ResearchTask to `accepted` or `in_progress` while it has an unsatisfied predecessor shall emit one warning line and shall proceed with the transition. The `transition_task` function shall compute this warning from the graph state as it stood before the write and return it to the caller, with the CLI printing it to stderr and the MCP tools appending it to their returned text; `walk_to_completed` shall accept an `on_warning` callback rather than returning a second value. The system shall provide a single `precedence_view()` computation that assembles precedence pairs, states, a `waits_on` map, a ready list, and chains in one pass, and `seldon task list`, `seldon_task_list`, `seldon briefing`, and `seldon go` shall all read readiness and chain data from this single computation. The `task list` command shall display a `WAITS_ON` column and mark as ready, with a `▸` marker, any open task with no unsatisfied predecessor. The `seldon go` and `seldon_go` commands shall render a 'Next ready' list in creation order and a 'Chains' list immediately after open tasks. A chain shall be defined as a weakly connected component of the `precedes` subgraph; a component of a single node shall not be rendered as a chain; a component forming a simple path shall render as `A → B → C`; a branching component shall not render as a single line and shall instead list its edges one per line. The `seldon verify` command shall include a Precedence check that fails when the `precedes` subgraph contains a cycle, a self-loop, or an edge whose endpoint is missing or is not a ResearchTask; this check is not Tier A, and default `seldon verify` shall exit with status 2 when this check fails. Cycle and self-loop detection for `precedes` shall run against the Neo4j graph projection rather than by replaying the event log.

parsed.statement: Document identity shall be defined as the content hash rather than the file path. Governed authored documents shall remain in place, with the path serving as the edit surface, because relocation breaks re-sync. Source documents such as PDFs, harvested pages, and thread exports shall be treated as immutable, may reside at any location, and shall be resolved by hash. Git shall hold governed markdown and shall not hold source blobs. parsed.statement: The Arnold coaching system shall implement a Decision Trace system that captures coaching decisions with full context, using the ADR-001 dual-storage pattern with Postgres storing decision trace facts (including trace_id, decision_type, decision_date, inputs_snapshot, policies_applied, conflicts_resolved, output_summary, outcome_type, outcome_id, approval_status, approved_by, approved_at, and tags) and Neo4j storing decision trace relationships (including HAD_DECISION, PRODUCED, CONSIDERED, INFORMED_BY, REFERENCED_PRECEDENT, and SUPERSEDED_BY) linked via trace_id and postgres_id. The Decision Trace system shall support decision types plan_generated, plan_adjusted, deviation_recorded, workout_skipped, intensity_override, constraint_applied, and goal_impact, each captured at a defined trigger point: create_workout_plan, user-requested plan modification, complete_with_deviations, skip_workout, manual RPE/load change, new injury/limitation, and goal progress update, respectively. The Decision Trace system shall receive trace emissions from the arnold-training MCP's create_workout_plan tool (plan_generated), complete_with_deviations tool (deviation_recorded), and skip_workout tool (workout_skipped); from the arnold-journal MCP's log_entry tool for severity concerning or higher (constraint_applied); and from the arnold-profile MCP's injury/constraint creation (constraint_applied). The Decision Trace system shall support precedent search via SQL queries against inputs_snapshot fields in Postgres and via Cypher queries against CONSIDERED relationships in Neo4j. The Decision Trace system shall enable inclusion of recent decision context in the coach brief.

parsed.statement: The HRR analysis pipeline shall compute direct HRR metrics (HRR30, HRR60, HRR_frac, early_slope) instead of tau; shall compute local pre-peak baseline as the median HR from -180s to -60s before peak rather than session minimum; shall apply a data quality filter requiring R² ≥ 0.75 for trend detection without winsorizing high outliers; shall compute a per-interval confidence score as 0.40×mag_score + 0.25×frac_score + 0.25×fit_score + 0.10×window_score, where mag_score = min(1.0, peak_minus_local / 13), frac_score = min(1.0, hrr_frac / 0.3), fit_score = R² from the exponential fit clamped 0-1, and window_score = 1.0 for windows ≥60s complete and degrading for shorter windows; shall compute weighted_HRR60 as HRR60 × confidence and use weighted_HRR60 rather than raw HRR60 for trend detectors; shall run a gap-aware EWMA with λ = 0.2 that resets to the stratum baseline when the gap since the prior measurement exceeds 48 hours; shall run a one-sided CUSUM detector for sustained declines with s_t = max(0, s_{t-1} + (baseline - x_t) - k), alerting when s_t ≥ h, using k = 0.5 × SDD and h = 4.0 × SDD, and resetting on a gap greater than 48 hours or on 3 or more consecutive values near baseline; shall maintain separate baseline and SDD statistics per training stratum (including STRENGTH and ENDURANCE); shall perform a dedicated weekly extended recovery protocol consisting of a final work set at 75-85% max HR followed immediately by 300 seconds of still supine recovery, recorded with protocol_type = 'dedicated' and recovery_posture = 'supine'; shall not mix supine and standing recovery data within the same EWMA and shall maintain separate baselines for each; and shall extract HR recovery intervals once into the hr_recovery_intervals table (extended per migration 014 with confidence, weighted_hrr60, actionable, recovery_posture, protocol_type, stratum, local_baseline_hr, peak_minus_local, early_slope, hr_180s, hr_300s, hrr180_abs, and hrr300_abs columns, plus an hrr_actionable view filtered on actionable = TRUE) and compute EWMA/CUSUM analyses on demand from that stored data rather than re-extracting from raw HR series each time.

The workout data schema shall use three tables named workouts, blocks, and sets, structured as workouts containing blocks containing sets, with blocks representing training-phase containers and sets representing atomic execution units unified across strength, endurance, and conditioning modalities via nullable columns. The sets table shall use a canonical distance_m (meters) column and a duration_s column for endurance data, superseding the prior distance plus distance_unit and pace columns as of 2026-08-05, with pace rendered from distance_m, duration_s, and sport_type by arnold.pace rather than stored. The blocks table shall have a modality column that optionally overrides workouts.sport_type, and block_type (warmup, main, accessory, conditioning, cooldown, circuit, emom, skill) shall be treated as orthogonal to modality. The sets table shall include a planned_set_id foreign key to planned_sets for deviation tracking, and deviation shall be computed via a view comparing executed sets against planned sets rather than enforced at logging time. Each of the workouts, blocks, and sets tables shall include an extra JSONB column as an escape hatch for ad-hoc fields, and frequently used extra keys shall be promoted to real columns via quarterly audit. Table names shall not use version prefixes such as "v2".

parsed.statement: The device telemetry architecture shall implement three layers: a human-authored workout log (workouts, blocks, sets), an immutable device telemetry layer (fit_files, fit_sessions, fit_records, polar_sessions, suunto_sessions, ultrahuman_daily), and a computed canonical metrics layer (canonical_metrics, daily_load_rollup, athlete_baselines), linked via a many-to-many workout_telemetry junction table with match confidence scores. The device telemetry architecture shall store vendor-provided metrics unchanged in vendor_metrics_json rather than treating them as universal metrics, and shall compute canonical metrics such as TRIMP, TSS, and HRR from raw samples (heart rate, power, pace) using documented, versioned formulas. Raw telemetry data shall be append-only, such that re-parsing a file creates a new version rather than overwriting prior data, and every computed metric shall link to its source file(s) or session(s), formula name and version, athlete parameters used, and computation timestamp. Athlete calibration parameters (HRmax, HRrest, FTP, threshold pace) shall be stored with timestamps and linked to the parameter set used for each metric computation. Device telemetry tables shall be organized by data source rather than by activity type.

parsed.statement: If a write operation cannot demonstrate its effect via read-back, then the system shall treat the operation as a failure regardless of whether the underlying calls threw an exception. The invariant shall apply immediately to log_workout, complete_as_written, complete_with_deviations, the Ultrahuman sync (scripts/sync/ultrahuman_to_postgres.py), and CC task closure (git↔Seldon), and all other write paths shall adopt the invariant as they are next touched. For PG↔Neo4j writes, the system shall write Postgres, write Neo4j, read back both, and fail loudly if either is missing; a scheduled reconciliation sweep shall independently diff the two stores to detect class-A bypass paths not owned by handlers. If the second store write fails, then the system shall flag the Postgres row as needs_graph_ref, the tool response shall state that condition exactly, and the reconciliation sweep shall repair the quarantine queue, without implementing a distributed transaction or rollback between Postgres and Neo4j. Write-tool success responses shall include observed effect (such as verified counts and read-back confirmation) rather than a bare success assertion.

parsed.statement: The self-learning system shall consist of 8 LLM agents (Arnold, Sparky, Bones, PT, Strength Assistant, Conditioning Assistant, Endurance Assistant, Critic/Learner) plus a deterministic Python engine (Planner, Selector, Progression, Validator), with Arnold as the sole user-facing agent, Sparky as the sole data-access tier for all database reads (Neo4j, Postgres, MCP tools) with provenance, Bones and PT reading via Sparky for medical/constraint and rehab/mobility surfacing respectively, the three specialist assistants consulted by the Planner for domain-specific session design, and the Critic/Learner processing five input streams (corrections, declarations, quantitative data, external knowledge, cross-day patterns) to draft rule proposals that always route through HITL approval rather than writing Rule nodes directly. The Python engine shall read from the knowledge store and write plans, and the Python engine shall never write to the knowledge store. The knowledge store shall be a hybrid of Neo4j, holding relationship-rich knowledge (Rule, Preference, Knowledge, Constraint, Observation nodes with SUPERSEDES, APPLIES_TO, DERIVED_FROM, EXPIRES_WHEN, PROMOTED_TO relationships), and Postgres, holding the event log and computed quantitative state (corrections, rule_proposals, promotion_history, quantitative_learnings, knowledge_imports tables). The learning loop shall use a single HITL gate across its five input streams: reactive corrections are extracted by Arnold into a corrections row and, if matching prior corrections beyond a threshold defaulting to 3 occurrences in 90 days, trigger the Critic to draft a proposal requiring user approval before a Rule node lands; declarative preferences detected by Arnold as volunteered (not reactive) shall result in a Preference node landing directly upon user confirmation, without entering the proposal queue; quantitative learning shall run as a weekly scheduled job computing per-exercise progression rates, per-block-type actual durations, and per-modality RPE/load relationships from the user's own data, written to quantitative_learnings without HITL; external knowledge scanning shall run as a weekly scheduled job plus manual triggers, with the Critic extracting claims into Knowledge nodes and Rule proposals requiring HITL approval before storage; cross-day pattern analysis shall run as a weekly scheduled job querying Postgres for correlations, with the Critic drafting structural Rule proposals with evidence requiring HITL approval before storage. The system shall ship with the knowledge store pre-populated via a seeding pipeline using the same Critic-extraction-to-HITL-approval plumbing as the learning loop, run as a batch over existing sources in the order: 301 existing Observation nodes, project docs (ADRs, handoffs, cc_tasks), form protocols and docs/research/, Wintermute library/, and external literature on-demand; after initial seeding completes for each source, that source shall switch to incremental mode rescanning only material newer than last_scanned_at. The data layer and seeding loop shall ship before the engine, in the build order: Phase 0 Foundation (schema, migrations, tests) with acceptance of round-trip writes/reads; Phase 1 seeding pipeline plus Critic skeleton plus observation seed with acceptance of 301 observations categorized and at least 50% approved; Phase 2 Engine (Planner/Selector/Progression/Validator) with acceptance of 10 consecutive 'arnold plan today' runs the user executes without rewriting; Phase 3 Specialist assistants with acceptance of the Conditioning Assistant returning MMA HIIT validated by the user; Phase 4 Arnold plus correction capture with acceptance of an end-to-end correction landing as a structured row; Phase 5 Critic active mode with acceptance of a correction on day N changing day N+1 generation; Phase 6, run in parallel with Phases 4–5, Dashboard surfaces with acceptance of pages rendering from the same tables; and Phase 7 remaining seed sources with acceptance of one reviewed batch per source.

parsed.statement: Every Cycle entity shall carry duration as an explicit stored start_date and end_date rather than an inferred length; cycle_type shall remain a duration-class label and not a length, so that a microcycle may range from 4 to 14 or more days. Code and tools shall not assume that the length of a microcycle equals 7 days, and week-based helpers such as end_date_for(weeks), describe().week, and week_count shall be treated as strength-convenience wrappers over day-based spans rather than as the underlying model. The week_type property shall remain a property of a microcycle regardless of its length, and shall be renamed to "microcycle designation" in documentation, with the underlying physical property name change deferred as a follow-up. Each modality shall select its own cycle cadence per plan, such as a 7-day cadence for lifting or a 10-14-day stimulus rotation for running, and no default cadence is chosen for either modality. parsed.statement: In the Seldon project graph, Result.name shall serve as the stable token key resolved by {{result:NAME:field}}, following the slug grammar ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.-]*$, case-sensitive, at most 128 characters, and unique per project graph, with any collision treated as a hard error naming the existing Result's artifact_id and no event written; the CLI shall require --name for new registrations via 'seldon result register', while the research.yaml property stays not required:true (category:system) so Results registered before this decision remain valid; units shall mean a real unit of measurement per seldon/domain/result_units_vocabulary.yaml, documented (not loaded) via docs/conventions/result_units_vocabulary.md. When a {{result:NAME:...}} token matches no name, the resolver shall fall back to matching a Result by units only if that units string is not in the vocabulary, and shall emit one warning line per fallback hit naming the token; this fallback is transitional, marked '# TRANSITIONAL (AD-028)' at its single definition site, and is to be removed once dependent projects migrate. The command 'seldon result migrate-names [--dry-run] [--project-dir]' shall classify every unnamed Result into exactly one of: migrated (units not a real unit and unique, so name:=units and units cleared), units_is_real_unit (leave alone), ambiguous (do not assign, listed for a human, when promoting would break name uniqueness or the string is both a real unit and a token key, each row reporting which condition applies), or no_units (leave alone); migration shall write one combined artifact_updated event rather than a bespoke event type, and shall never mutate the graph directly. An unknown --data-name, --script-name, --script-id, or --script-path shall be a hard error with non-zero exit and no event written, with every reference resolved and validated before any graph mutation; 'seldon result backfill-provenance --map FILE [--dry-run]' shall repair existing graphs by emitting computed_from/generated_by link events, where an unknown name fails only that row, processing continues for the rest, and the command reports at the end with a non-zero exit if any row failed.
